Q1

Introduction

[Introduction text]

1.1

As explained in the help file (?SaratogaHouses), the SaratogaHouses data set contains data about many houses from Saratoga County, New York in the year 2006. Suppose a family is in search of a home that was 1) newly constructed and that has 2) three bedrooms. Suppose further that they are trying to decide how big of a livingArea they can afford and whether or not the price of the home is significantly impacted by adding a fireplace to their “dream home” wish list.

# 1.1
palette(c("grey","firebrick"))

SH2 <- filter(SaratogaHouses, bedrooms == 3,  newConstruction=="Yes") %>% 
  mutate(fireplace = ifelse(fireplaces > 0, 1,0))

plot(price ~ livingArea,
     data = SH2,
     col = as.factor(fireplace),
     main = "Saratoga Houses - Ideal Home",
     xlab = "Living Area",
     ylab = "Price",
     pch = 16)


legend("topleft",
       legend = c("No Fireplace","Fireplace"),
       col = c("grey","firebrick"),
       pch = 16,
       bty = "n")

mylm <- lm(price ~ livingArea + fireplace + livingArea:fireplace, data = SH2)
summary(mylm) %>% pander()
  Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)
(Intercept) -12290 59660 -0.206 0.8392
livingArea 103.1 32.43 3.178 0.005499
fireplace -116723 74519 -1.566 0.1357
livingArea:fireplace 74.75 37.94 1.97 0.06535
Fitting linear model: price ~ livingArea + fireplace + livingArea:fireplace
Observations Residual Std. Error \(R^2\) Adjusted \(R^2\)
21 27707 0.8955 0.8771 
abline(mylm$coefficients["(Intercept)"], 
       mylm$coefficients["livingArea"], col=palette()[1])

abline(mylm$coefficients["(Intercept)"] + mylm$coefficients["fireplace"], 
       mylm$coefficients["livingArea"] + mylm$coefficients["livingArea:fireplace"], col=palette()[2])

1.2

Let’s diagnose the appropriateness of using a linear model for the data.

# 1.2
par(mfrow=c(1,3))

plot(mylm, which=1)
qqPlot(mylm$residuals, id=FALSE)
plot(mylm$residuals)

aq <- airquality

summary(mylm) %>% pander()
  Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)

I(Month^2) -3.283 0.3199 -10.26 4.737e-19
Fitting linear model: Temp ~ Month + I(Month^2)
Observations Residual Std. Error \(R^2\) Adjusted \(R^2\)
153 6.624 0.5166 0.5102 
par(mfrow=c(1,3))

plot(mylm, which=1)

plot(mylm$residuals)

par(mfrow = c(1,1)) #This resets your plotting window for future plots.
2.2
# 2.2
july_fourth = 7.129032

mylm <- lm(Temp ~ Month + I(Month^2), data = aq)
summary(mylm) %>% pander()
  Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)
(Intercept) -95.73 15.24 -6.281 3.458e-09
Month 48.72 4.489 10.85 1.29e-20
I(Month^2) -3.283 0.3199 -10.26 4.737e-19
Fitting linear model: Temp ~ Month + I(Month^2)
Observations Residual Std. Error \(R^2\) Adjusted \(R^2\)
153 6.624 0.5166 0.5102 
# Estimate  Std. Error  t value Pr(>|t|)
# (Intercept)   -95.73  15.24   -6.281  3.458e-09
# Month 48.72   4.489   10.85   1.29e-20
# I(Month^2)    -3.283  0.3199  -10.26  4.737e-19

temp_july_fourth <- 
  (mylm$coefficients["(Intercept)"]) + 
  (mylm$coefficients["Month"] * july_fourth) +
  (july_fourth^2) * mylm$coefficients["I(Month^2)"]

# The average temperature on July 4th.
temp_july_fourth
## (Intercept) 
##    84.74588
2.3
# 2.3
plot(Temp ~ Month, data = aq, col="skyblue2", pch = 19, main = "airquality Data Set")

curve(predict(mylm, data.frame(Month = x)), add=TRUE, col="skyblue2", lwd=2)

lines(c(july_fourth, july_fourth), c(0, temp_july_fourth), lty=2, col="firebrick")

lines(c(0, july_fourth), c(temp_july_fourth, temp_july_fourth), lty=2, col="firebrick")

points(july_fourth, temp_july_fourth, cex=1.2, col="firebrick", pch = 19)

text(july_fourth + .15, temp_july_fourth + .2 , "Predicted Temp", cex=0.5, pos=3)

2.4

This formula is how we identify the vertex of the quadratic line. It’s not always meaningful but sometimes it is.

\[ \frac{-\beta_1}{2\cdot\beta_2} \]

The x value of the vertex is:

# 2.4
vertex_x <- -(mylm$coefficients["Month"]) / (2 * mylm$coefficients["I(Month^2)"])
vertex_x
##    Month 
## 7.420204
2.5

The y value of the vertex is:

# 2.5
vertex_y <- 
  (mylm$coefficients["(Intercept)"]) + 
  (mylm$coefficients["Month"] * vertex_x +
  (vertex_x^2) * mylm$coefficients["I(Month^2)"])
vertex_y
## (Intercept) 
##     85.0242

4.1
# 4.1
?faithful
4.2

Perform a simple linear regression to determine if the expected waiting time to the next eruption can be modeled by the length of the previous eruption.

# 4.2
mylm <- lm(waiting ~ eruptions, data = faithful)
summary(mylm) %>% pander()
  Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)
(Intercept) 33.47 1.155 28.99 7.136e-85
eruptions 10.73 0.3148 34.09 8.13e-100
Fitting linear model: waiting ~ eruptions
Observations Residual Std. Error \(R^2\) Adjusted \(R^2\)
272 5.914 0.8115 0.8108
4.3
# 4.3
plot(waiting ~ eruptions, data = faithful)
abline(mylm)

4.4
# 4.4
par(mfrow=c(1,2))
plot(mylm, which=1:2)

par(mfrow = c(1,1)) #This resets your plotting window for future plots.
4.5

If the erruption is 3.5 minutes we would expect the visitor to wait in minutes about:

# 4.5
yint <-  33.47
increase <- 10.73
t = 3.5

wait_time <- yint + (t * increase)
wait_time
